hero.title:
Trucks are cubes on wheels.
We make them slip through the air.
hero.text: Y-stream is a textile aerodynamic device for semi-trailers. It inflates with the airflow, cuts drag by 15 % and fuel consumption by up to 10 %. Patented, validated in the wind tunnel, ready to scale.

problem.title:
Regulation shaped the truck.
Physics pays the bill.
problem.text: European size limits turned trailers into boxes: the most efficient shape for loading, the worst for moving through air. A flat rear face creates a wide zone of turbulence and low pressure behind the vehicle, the wake, that literally pulls the truck backwards.

of that drag is generated by the rear of the trailer alone

problem.caption: Wake turbulence behind a box-shaped trailer (CFD simulation)

idea.title: A tail that inflates itself
idea.text: Y-stream is a textile appendage fitted to the rear of the trailer. Above 80 km/h the relative wind inflates it into a streamlined tail that closes the wake. The inflation is purely mechanical, no motor, no electronics, and adjusts with speed. Below 80 km/h it stays flat and the trailer keeps its standard dimensions.

points.title: Profiles the rear
points.text: The tail extends the trailer's shape and lets the air close smoothly behind it.

points.title: Inflated by the airflow
points.text: Mechanical, self-adjusting inflation driven by the relative wind. Nothing to switch on.

points.title: Doors, loading and footprint: unchanged
points.text: The patented mount never gets in the way: rear doors open and close normally, loading and unloading operations are untouched, and the trailer keeps its regulatory dimensions and footprint.

points.title: Born from free flight
points.text: The concept comes from our experience of paragliding wings and harnesses: light textile structures shaped by air.

idea.caption: The inflated tail closes the wake and reduces drag

steps.title: Standard
steps.text: Fitted on new trailers or retrofitted on existing ones, with a minimal aluminium technical frame.

steps.title: Inactive below 80 km/h
steps.text: In town and during manoeuvres the device stays flat against the rear doors.

steps.title: Self-inflating
steps.text: At motorway speed the airflow inflates the textile pocket into its aerodynamic shape.

steps.title: Lower consumption
steps.text: Drag drops, fuel consumption follows, directly, for every kilometre driven.

items.title: total drag
items.text: Measured in wind-tunnel campaigns on 1/6-scale models, up to 10 % less energy consumed.

items.title: safety
items.text: Soft and non-blunt, the tail acts like an airbag and increases the safety distance behind the trailer.

items.title: fits the fleet
items.text: Trailer dimensions are standardised across Europe: one design, mass production, quick installation.

items.title: compliant
items.text: Designed for the new European directive on heavy-vehicle aerodynamics, to which we contribute.

development.title: Regulation, design, manufacturing, tests: done
development.text: To make the project viable we created the company ease lab SAS, which carried all the first stages. Materials, technology choices and operating principles have been validated on 1/6-scale prototypes.
